beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Access may arrive through services and shared fleets before individual ownership becomes common.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These are conditional scenarios, not guarantees about when a particular household receives a robot.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The detailed cost discussion shows what evidence would make the scenario more credible.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Even successful material sufficiency would leave time, attention, and particular places limited.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Other people’s consent cannot become a resource distributed by a more productive economy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Nor can everyone occupy the highest position in the same hierarchy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book therefore separates a universal material floor from the end of competition.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its human chapters consider motivation, belonging, prestige, and the persistence of domination.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They avoid assuming that abundance automatically turns people into a different species.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That qualification protects the central promise from becoming a fantasy of universal satisfaction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The political chapters return to the home at the end of the supply chain.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Who owns the infrastructure, and under what conditions can people use its services?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: More production can coexist with concentrated power or access tied to surveillance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The author argues for institutions that turn capability into a resilient floor of provision.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The timeline remains conditional on construction, ecological conditions, conflict, and distribution.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its estimates are scenarios to revise, rather than precise institutional forecasts.
